name: Proto-Human (hypothetical)
description: Hypothetical and highly speculative single ancestor of all human languages; not accepted by mainstream historical linguistics.

name: Proto-Indo-European
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Indo-European family.

name: Proto-Anatolian
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Anatolian branch; earliest IE branch to split off.

name: Hittite
description: Oldest attested Indo-European language; written in cuneiform.

name: Luwian
description: Sister language to Hittite; attested in cuneiform and hieroglyphic scripts.

name: Lydian
description: Iron-age Anatolian language of the Lydian kingdom.

name: Proto-Tocharian
description: Reconstructed ancestor of Tocharian A and B.

name: Tocharian A
description: Eastern Tocharian; liturgical language preserved in Buddhist texts.

name: Tocharian B
description: Western Tocharian; more widely attested than Tocharian A.

name: Proto-Indo-Iranian
description: Reconstructed common ancestor of Indo-Aryan and Iranian languages.

name: Classical Sanskrit
description: Standardized literary language codified by Pāṇini.

name: Pali
description: Middle Indo-Aryan; liturgical language of Theravada Buddhism.

name: Prakrit (Middle Indo-Aryan)
description: Vernacular Middle Indo-Aryan languages; ancestor of modern Indo-Aryan tongues.

name: Apabhraṃśa
description: Late Middle Indo-Aryan stage transitional to modern languages.

name: Hindi
description: Modern standard register of Khariboli; written in Devanagari.

name: Urdu
description: Persianized register of Khariboli; written in Perso-Arabic script.

name: Bengali
description: Eastern Indo-Aryan language of Bangladesh and West Bengal.

name: Punjabi
description: Indo-Aryan language of the Punjab region; tonal.

name: Nepali
description: Eastern Pahari language; official language of Nepal.

name: Sinhala
description: Insular Indo-Aryan language of Sri Lanka.

name: Romani
description: Indo-Aryan language of the Roma people.

name: Kashmiri
description: Dardic language; sometimes grouped within Indo-Aryan.

name: Old Persian
description: Royal language of the Achaemenid Empire.

name: Persian (Farsi)
description: New Persian; written in Perso-Arabic script.

name: Tajik
description: Tajik variety of Persian; written in Cyrillic.

name: Kurdish
description: Northwestern Iranian dialect continuum (Kurmanji, Sorani, etc.).

name: Scythian
description: Eastern Iranian language of the Scythian nomads.

name: Sogdian
description: Eastern Iranian Silk Road lingua franca.

name: Proto-Greek
description: Reconstructed ancestor of all Greek varieties.

name: Mycenaean Greek
description: Earliest attested Greek; written in Linear B.

name: Ancient Greek
description: Classical Greek of Homer, Plato, and Aristotle.

name: Koine Greek
description: Lingua franca of the Hellenistic and early Roman world; language of the New Testament and Septuagint.

name: Proto-Italic
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Italic languages.

name: Umbrian
description: Sabellic Italic language; attested in the Iguvine Tablets.

name: Vulgar Latin
description: Spoken Latin of the late empire; ancestor of the Romance languages.

name: Old French
description: Langues d'oïl varieties of medieval France.

name: Middle French
description: Transitional stage between Old and Modern French.

name: Occitan
description: Langue d'oc; medieval language of the troubadours.

name: Galician
description: Ibero-Romance language closely related to Portuguese.

name: Italian
description: Standard Italian based on the Tuscan dialect.

name: Venetian
description: Italo-Romance language of the Venetian region.

name: Neapolitan
description: Italo-Romance language of Naples and southern Italy.

name: Dalmatian
description: Extinct Romance language; last speaker died 1898.

name: Proto-Celtic
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Celtic languages.

name: Gaulish
description: Continental Celtic language of ancient Gaul.

name: Celtiberian
description: Continental Celtic language of pre-Roman Iberia.

name: Proto-Brittonic
description: Ancestor of the Brittonic Celtic languages.

name: Cornish
description: Brittonic Celtic language; revived in the 20th century.

name: Primitive Irish
description: Earliest attested Goidelic Celtic; ogham inscriptions.

name: Old Irish
description: Goidelic Celtic of early medieval Ireland.

name: Middle Irish
description: Transitional Goidelic Celtic; common ancestor of Irish, Scottish Gaelic, and Manx.

name: Proto-Germanic
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Germanic languages.

name: Gothic
description: East Germanic language; preserved in Wulfila's Bible translation.

name: Proto-Norse
description: Earliest North Germanic stage; runic inscriptions.

name: Old Norse
description: Language of the Vikings; ancestor of modern North Germanic languages.

name: Norwegian
description: North Germanic language; Bokmål and Nynorsk standards.

name: Norn
description: Extinct North Germanic language of the Northern Isles.

name: Old English
description: West Germanic language of Anglo-Saxon England.

name: Middle English
description: English of Chaucer's era; heavy Norman French influence.

name: Early Modern English
description: English of Shakespeare and the King James Bible.

name: Scots
description: West Germanic language closely related to English.

name: Old Frisian
description: West Germanic language closely related to Old English.

name: Frisian
description: West Germanic language; closest living relative of English.

name: Old Saxon
description: West Germanic ancestor of Low German.

name: Afrikaans
description: West Germanic language descended from 17th-century Dutch.

name: Yiddish
description: High German language with Hebrew, Aramaic, and Slavic elements.

name: Pennsylvania German
description: West Central German variety spoken by Amish and Mennonites.

name: Luxembourgish
description: Moselle Franconian variety; national language of Luxembourg.

name: Proto-Balto-Slavic
description: Reconstructed common ancestor of Baltic and Slavic languages.

name: Proto-Slavic
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Slavic languages.

name: Old Church Slavonic
description: First literary Slavic language; liturgical language of the Slavic Orthodox churches.

name: Old East Slavic
description: Ancestor of Russian, Ukrainian, and Belarusian.

name: Serbo-Croatian
description: South Slavic dialect continuum (Serbian, Croatian, Bosnian, Montenegrin).

name: Classical Armenian (Grabar)
description: Liturgical language of the Armenian Apostolic Church.

name: Albanian
description: Isolate branch of Indo-European; Gheg and Tosk dialect groups.

name: Proto-Afroasiatic
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Afroasiatic phylum.

name: Proto-Semitic
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Semitic languages.

name: Akkadian
description: East Semitic language; written in cuneiform; included Babylonian and Assyrian.

name: Phoenician
description: Canaanite language; alphabet ancestral to most modern scripts.

name: Biblical Hebrew
description: Canaanite Semitic language of the Hebrew Bible.

name: Hebrew
description: Modern Hebrew; revived as a spoken language in the late 19th/early 20th century.

name: Aramaic
description: Northwest Semitic language; lingua franca of much of the ancient Near East.

name: Syriac
description: Christian literary form of Eastern Aramaic.

name: Neo-Aramaic
description: Modern Aramaic dialect cluster (Assyrian, Chaldean, Turoyo, etc.).

name: Classical Arabic
description: Language of the Qur'an and classical Arabic literature.

name: Levantine Arabic
description: Arabic dialect group of Syria, Lebanon, Palestine, Jordan.

name: Maghrebi Arabic
description: Arabic dialect group of the Maghreb.

name: Gulf Arabic
description: Arabic dialect group of the Gulf states.

name: Maltese
description: Semitic language descended from Maghrebi Arabic; written in Latin script.

name: Amharic
description: South Semitic language; official language of Ethiopia.

name: Ancient Egyptian
description: Earliest stages of Egyptian; hieroglyphic, hieratic, and demotic scripts.

name: Coptic
description: Final stage of Egyptian; liturgical language of the Coptic Church.

name: Hausa
description: Chadic language; major West African lingua franca.

name: Proto-Sino-Tibetan
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Sino-Tibetan family.

name: Old Chinese
description: Language of oracle bone inscriptions and early classical texts.

name: Middle Chinese
description: Chinese of the Sui-Tang period; basis of Sinoxenic vocabulary.

name: Mandarin Chinese
description: Largest Sinitic variety; basis of Standard Chinese.

name: Dzongkha
description: South Tibetic language; official language of Bhutan.

name: Newar
description: Tibeto-Burman language with long literary tradition.

name: Proto-Dravidian
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Dravidian family.

name: Proto-Uralic
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Uralic family.

name: Mansi
description: Ugric Uralic language; closest relative of Hungarian.

name: Proto-Turkic
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Turkic family.

name: Ottoman Turkish
description: Persianized literary Turkic; written in Arabic script.

name: Turkish
description: Modern Turkish; reformed and written in Latin script.

name: Tuvan
description: Siberian Turkic language; known for throat singing.

name: Proto-Mongolic
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Mongolic family.

name: Middle Mongol
description: Language of the Mongol Empire; Secret History of the Mongols.

name: Mongolian
description: Khalkha Mongolian; written in Cyrillic and traditional Mongolian scripts.

name: Proto-Tungusic
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Tungusic family.

name: Manchu
description: Tungusic language of the Qing dynasty; now critically endangered.

name: Proto-Koreanic
description: Reconstructed ancestor of Korean; relationship to other families disputed.

name: Old Korean
description: Korean of the Three Kingdoms and Unified Silla periods.

name: Middle Korean
description: Korean of the Goryeo and early Joseon; first written in Hangul (1443).

name: Korean
description: Modern Korean; isolate or small family depending on classification.

name: Jeju
description: Koreanic language; not mutually intelligible with mainland Korean.

name: Proto-Japonic
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Japonic family.

name: Old Japanese
description: Earliest attested stage of Japanese; Man'yōshū.

name: Middle Japanese
description: Early and Late Middle Japanese; classical literary language.

name: Proto-Austronesian
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Austronesian family.

name: Proto-Malayo-Polynesian
description: Ancestor of all Austronesian languages outside Taiwan.

name: Tagalog (Filipino)
description: Philippine Austronesian language; basis of Filipino.

name: Malay
description: Western Malayo-Polynesian language; basis of Bahasa Malaysia and Bahasa Indonesia.

name: Indonesian
description: Standardized register of Malay; national language of Indonesia.

name: Javanese
description: Austronesian language with long literary tradition.

name: Malagasy
description: Austronesian language; closest relatives are Barito languages of Borneo.

name: Proto-Tai-Kadai
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Kra-Dai (Tai-Kadai) family.

name: Proto-Austroasiatic
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Austroasiatic family.

name: Proto-Niger-Congo
description: Hypothesized ancestor of the Niger-Congo macrofamily; internal coherence debated.

name: Proto-Bantu
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Bantu languages.

name: Swahili
description: Sabaki Bantu language; major lingua franca of East Africa.

name: Xhosa
description: Nguni Bantu language; click consonants from Khoisan contact.

name: Lingala
description: Bantu lingua franca of the Congo River basin.

name: Kongo
description: Bantu language of the Kongo people.

name: San (Tuu and Kx'a languages)
description: Click-language families of the San peoples.

name: Sandawe
description: Click language; sometimes grouped with Khoe.

name: Proto-Northeast Caucasian
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Northeast Caucasian (Nakh-Daghestanian) family.

name: Proto-Northwest Caucasian
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Northwest Caucasian family.

name: Abkhaz
description: Northwest Caucasian language with extreme consonant inventory.

name: Ubykh
description: Extinct Northwest Caucasian language; famous for ~84 consonants.

name: Proto-Kartvelian
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Kartvelian family.

name: Georgian
description: Kartvelian language with its own script.

name: Basque (Euskara)
description: Language isolate of the western Pyrenees.

name: Sumerian
approxDate: c. 3000–2000 BCE (spoken); literary use to c. 100 CE

name: Elamite
description: Language isolate; one of the three official languages of the Achaemenid Empire.

name: Iberian
description: Unclassified pre-Roman language of eastern Spain.

name: Nivkh (Gilyak)
description: Language isolate of the Russian Far East.

name: Ket
description: Last surviving Yeniseian language; possibly related to Na-Dené.

name: Kalaallisut (Greenlandic)
description: West Greenlandic; official language of Greenland.

name: Proto-Algic
description: Reconstructed ancestor of Algic; includes Algonquian + Yurok + Wiyot.

name: Proto-Algonquian
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Algonquian languages.

name: Proto-Iroquoian
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Iroquoian family.

name: Cherokee
description: Sole Southern Iroquoian language; Sequoyah syllabary.

name: Proto-Siouan
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Siouan family.

name: Proto-Uto-Aztecan
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Uto-Aztecan family.

name: Proto-Mayan
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Mayan family.

name: Classic Maya
description: Language of the Classic Maya inscriptions.

name: Proto-Quechuan
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Quechuan languages.

name: Classical Quechua
description: Lingua franca of the Inca Empire.

name: Quechua
description: Modern Quechua dialect continuum (Cuzco, Ayacucho, etc.).

name: Proto-Pama-Nyungan
description: Reconstructed ancestor of the Pama-Nyungan family.

name: Tok Pisin
description: English-based creole; national language of Papua New Guinea.

name: Papiamento
description: Iberian-based creole with Dutch and African elements.

name: Esperanto
description: International auxiliary language created by L. L. Zamenhof.

name: Interlingua
description: International auxiliary language based on Romance roots.

name: Klingon
description: Constructed language created by Marc Okrand.

name: Quenya
description: Elvish language created by J.R.R. Tolkien.

name: Sindarin
description: Elvish language created by J.R.R. Tolkien.

name: American Sign Language
description: Sign language descended from French Sign Language.

name: British Sign Language
description: Sign language; ancestor of Australian and New Zealand Sign Languages.

name: French Sign Language (LSF)
description: Sign language; ancestor of ASL and many other national sign languages.
